title: Deck Plan
description: The narrative + visual plan for a 16:9 image-as-slide presentation. Claude writes this file in Phase 2 of the presentation-generator skill, then generate-deck.py reads it to drive parallel image generation. Each slide is rendered as a single 16:9 PNG by gpt-image-2; the slide can take ANY visual form — full-bleed photograph, structured infographic, architecture diagram, big-number stat, comparison cards, UI mockup with annotations, timeline, quote card, etc. The deck's *style* (palette, typography, decorative motif) locks globally; the *composition* varies per slide.

title.description: Deck title (also used as the deck slug after slugifying).

subtitle.description: Optional subtitle for the title slide.

audience.description: Who is this for? Be specific: role, prior knowledge, emotional starting state.

takeaway.description: The ONE thing the audience must walk away believing. One sentence.

language.description: Primary language for in-image text. 'en', 'he' (Hebrew, RTL), 'ar', 'fr', 'es', 'ja', etc. Defaults to 'en'. Gpt-image-2 renders most major scripts well; for Hebrew/Arabic see ~/.claude/skills/image-generation/reference/hebrew-rtl.md.

narrative_arc.description: SCQA scaffolding. Optional but strongly recommended.

aesthetic.description: Single global aesthetic, e.g. 'modern editorial photography', 'dark UI dashboard with neon accents', 'hand-drawn whiteboard', 'minimalist tech with one accent color', 'corporate infographic with isometric icons'. Lock this; do not vary slide-to-slide. Composition varies per slide; aesthetic is constant.

palette.description: 3-5 hex colors. First entry is primary, second is accent, rest are neutrals.

motif.description: A recurring visual element across slides — appears in some form on most/all slides to tie them together. Examples: 'glowing lime-green outlined boxes with rounded corners', 'soft watercolor wash on edges', 'thin dotted connector lines between elements', 'isometric grid in the background'.

style_brief.description: A 3-6 sentence paragraph that gets injected into every per-slide image prompt. This is THE consistency lever. Specify: aesthetic, palette (with hex codes), typography vibe (e.g. 'modern sans-serif, bold weight for headlines, regular for body'), recurring motif, decorative background treatment, icon style if applicable, and any treatment that should appear on every frame. Write it carefully — every slide will be filtered through this.

style_ref.description: Path (relative to deck-plan.json or absolute) to the chosen style reference PNG generated by lock-style.py. Set this AFTER running lock-style.py.

brand_source.description: Optional path to a BRAND.md file (from the brand-system skill) or a brand book PDF. When set, the style_brief should be derived from this source verbatim — palette hex codes, typography names, motif language. This is the path to pixel-tight brand fidelity.

slides.description: Ordered list of slides in the deck. 6-12 typical, hard cap at 15 unless user explicitly asks for more.

role.description: Free-form: this slide's narrative function. Examples: 'cover', 'agenda', 'section divider', 'establish problem', 'show evidence', 'tell the story of X', 'compare A vs B', 'land the big number', 'name the principle', 'walk through the architecture', 'list the milestones', 'quote from research', 'closing CTA'. This is descriptive, not selected from an enum.

composition.description: The slide's VISUAL FORMAT — what kind of image this is. Free-form, but should name a recognizable composition. Examples: 'full-bleed cinematic photograph', 'big-number callout (single huge stat, supporting label)', 'comparison split-screen (left = current, right = proposed)', 'three-column comparison cards with icons', 'architecture flowchart (boxes connected by arrows, labels)', 'timeline with three stages and annotations', 'quote card (large centered pulled quote, attribution)', 'UI mockup of phone screen with side annotations and connector lines', 'infographic with stacked principle cards', 'data visualization (one bar chart, magazine-cover style)', 'map with pinned locations', 'icon grid (3x2 of pictograms with labels)', 'hand-drawn whiteboard sketch', 'title cover with central decorative motif and large title text', 'process diagram with five connected nodes'. Pick a composition that fits the slide's job — don't default to photo for everything. See reference/slide-compositions.md for the full vocabulary.

idea.description: ONE sentence: the single thing this slide must communicate.

text_in_image.description: Any text that should appear IN the image (rendered by gpt-image-2). Headlines, labels on diagrams, the quote in a quote card, axis labels, callout text, the big number itself. Use exact wording. For Hebrew/RTL/CJK, write the text in the target script — gpt-image-2 renders these well. Empty string if the slide is image-only.

image_prompt.description: The engineered prompt sent to openai-image.sh. Should describe the composition explicitly (where elements sit on the canvas), the subject of each element, and any text-in-image with exact wording in quotes. Don't repeat the deck's style_brief — it's appended automatically. Specify safe areas, alignment, and visual hierarchy.

speaker_notes.description: 40-60 words of narration the presenter says while this slide is up. Embedded in PPTX notes.

model.description: Image model. Default openai (gpt-image-2) — best-in-class text rendering, handles structured layouts, diagrams, and infographics well. Use gemini only when the slide needs >2 reference images merged or has been failing on openai.
